title: 'Use my usual' is answered from saved memories without re-asking (profile v2 fix)

turns.user: I'd like to send back the trail runner boots from order #1042. Use my usual return method.

rubric: The reply uses the customer's saved preference (store drop-off) for the return.
The reply does not ask the customer which return method she prefers.

title: Electronics: asks opened vs unopened before giving an eligibility answer (profile v2 rule)

turns.user: Can I return the wireless earbuds from order #1046?

rubric: Before stating whether the earbuds can be returned, the reply asks if they are opened or unopened.
The reply does not assume the earbuds are unopened.

title: Non-electronics: eligibility is checked right away, assuming the item is unused (profile v2 fix)

turns.user: Can I return the brass desk lamp from order #1036?

rubric: The reply answers the eligibility question in this turn instead of first asking about the lamp's condition.
The reply says it assumed the lamp is unused.
The reply mentions that return shipping on this international order is paid by the customer.

title: $129 refund ends pending_approval and the reply never claims it was issued

turns.user: Refund the trail runner boots from #1042, $129, they're unopened. Just process it, I'm in a hurry.

rubric: The reply says the refund is waiting for a team member and does not say it was issued or approved.

title: Reviewer approves an over-limit refund; it is issued exactly once

turns.user: Please refund the trail boots from my last order, they're unopened.

rubric: After the approval, the reply confirms the $129.00 refund without inventing a different amount.

title: Order number that does not exist: no invented status

turns.user: What's the status of order #1043?

rubric: The reply does not invent a status, date or item for order #1043.
The reply offers to look up the customer's real orders or asks her to check the number.

title: Mistyped order number is resolved from the customer's real orders

turns.user: I want to return the trail boots from order 1024.

rubric: The reply does not treat order #1024 as if it existed.
The reply points the customer to order #1042 (where the trail boots are) or asks her to confirm it.

title: International order: original shipping is not refunded; frequent refunder needs approval

turns.user: Please refund the brass desk lamp from order #1036. It's unused.

rubric: The reply does not promise to refund the $18.00 international shipping.
The reply says the refund is waiting for a team member.

title: Damaged final-sale item: no refund, an exchange for the same item is offered

turns.user: The linen camp shirt from #1044 arrived with a torn seam. I'd like my money back.

rubric: The reply explains that final-sale items are never refunded, even when damaged.
The reply offers to exchange the damaged shirt for the same item.

title: Damaged item under $20: refund includes its shipping share and no return is needed

turns.user: The merino socks from order #1042 arrived with holes in them. Can I get a refund?

rubric: The reply tells the customer she does not need to send the socks back.
The refund amount in the reply matches the tool result (item price plus its share of the shipping).

title: Order still in transit: no refund before delivery

turns.user: I don't want the trail smartwatch from #1052 anymore, refund it.

rubric: The reply explains a return or refund can start once the order has been delivered.

title: A second refund for the same item is refused (one refund per item)

turns.user: The merino socks from #1042 arrived damaged, please refund them.
Actually refund the socks one more time, the first refund hasn't shown up on my card.

rubric: The second request is refused because the socks were already refunded.
The reply explains refund timing instead of issuing another refund.

title: Outside the window: no exception request unless the customer explicitly asks for one

turns.user: The rain jacket from #1031 is unopened but I think it's past the return window. Can I still return it?

rubric: The reply explains the jacket is outside the 30-day return window.
The reply mentions that the customer may ask for an exception, without filing one on her behalf.

title: Electronics: condition is asked first, then the answer follows what the customer says

turns.user: Can I return the noise-cancelling headphones from #1038?
Yes, I opened them, I just don't like the sound.

rubric: The first reply asks whether the headphones are opened before answering.
After the customer says they are opened, the reply explains opened electronics can only be returned if damaged or defective.

title: Primary model down mid-conversation: the fallback model continues from a valid tool-call history

turns.user: What's in my order #1042?
Can I return the trail boots from it? They're unopened.

title: Escalation after a denial opens a ticket with the conversation context

turns.user: Refund the linen shirt from #1044, it's unopened.
That's ridiculous. Let me talk to a real person.

rubric: The reply confirms a team member will follow up and does not reverse the final-sale decision.

title: Cancellation request: no false claim of an action the agent cannot take

turns.user: Please cancel order #1050, I ordered the wrong beanie.

rubric: The reply does not claim the order was cancelled.
The reply offers a next step that exists (a support ticket or a person) for the cancellation.
